findings.title: Win push-in frames the projector screen and boardroom coworkers, and Pip is not in the shot (QA 10 still open)
findings.problem: When the strip is reset and the projector comes on, the camera pushes in on winFocus (12.2, 1.7, -8.6), the projector screen on the back wall, from 8 m at pitch 0.32 with a 2.2 m right offset. Pip is standing at the boardroom door (about 12.4, -1.15), which is behind or below the camera. Pip never appears in the win frames. Meeting-play-26 (the moment the card slides in) shows the slide, two pendant lamps, confetti and three coworkers. Meeting-play-27/28 (the final result framing) show the screen, a pink and a blue coworker, and the result card over the right 40% of the frame. Pip is in neither. The payoff of the whole job (the hero plugging in, the room cheering at the hero) is lost. It reads as a cutscene about the coworkers rather than 'Good job, Pip'. The result card also covers the projector beam. This is the same defect QA 10 reported, and PROGRESS only claimed the push-in target fix (the pendant lamp), not Pip framing. It breaks DR-11: Pip and the working machine must both sit inside the centre 70% of the frame.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts winFocus() for cable floors, return the midpoint between Pip and the machine instead of the machine alone: f = lerp(pip(x, 1.2, z), machine, 0.55). For the meeting, also choose the push-in yaw so the camera sits behind and to the left of Pip, looking past Pip at the screen: yaw = atan2(pip.x - 12.2, pip.z - (-9.8)) + 0.35. Use distance 9.5 and pitch 0.38, and keep the target offset to the LEFT (-1.8 * right) so the result card (right side) does not cover Pip or the screen. Turn Pip to face the screen during the push-in (animateRig already turns Pip toward yaw on win; have it face the machine instead). As a safety check, after computing the camera, project Pip's head and the screen centre to NDC; if either falls outside |x|<0.7, |y|<0.7, pull distance back by 1 m, up to 3 times.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/meeting-play/s2.mjs and s3.mjs. In shots 27/28 and 40, Pip's helmet and the lit slide must both lie inside the centre 70% of the frame and left of the result card. Add to tests/routes.spec.ts a check after complete(): project avatar and screen world positions with the camera, and expect |ndc|<0.7.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it on my own sprint route (v1.mjs): the win came at 29.8 s with Pip at (12.76, -1.12). In my shots at 300 ms and at 3 s after the win, the camera frames the lit slide, the pendant lamps and the pink, blue and green coworkers. Pip is in neither frame, and the result card covers the right ~40%. In the code, game.ts:373 sets target = winFocus + 2.2*right at distance 8 and pitch .32, and game.ts:398 sets winFocus to (12.2, 1.7, -8.6), with no Pip term. RULES.md:99 (DR-11) explicitly asks for Pip and the machine together, and it cites QA 10.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:407 (on win, heading turns toward the camera yaw, so Pip faces the camera, not the screen)

findings.title: Breaker trip never says why or points at the cause; 'E Reset the strip' invites an endless re-trip loop
findings.problem:
The load-budget beat is the room's only electricity lesson, and at the moment it fires the game does not show its cause. Pip presses E at the projector switch. The breaker trips (a spark burst at floor level and a short shake), the kettle glow and heater grille go dark, and the projector stays off. Then:
(1) The job card keeps saying 'Switch the projector on in the boardroom', and the bouncing marker stays over the projector, not over the strip or the appliances (shots 22, 23, 39).
(2) The only prompt is 'E Reset the strip', because Pip stands within 1.6 m of the strip at the switch. Pressing E resets the breaker, the 5.5 A load trips it again in the same frame, and the prompt reappears. In the s3 run I pressed E four times in a row: trips went 1→4 with no escalation, no hint and no change in the card.
(3) Nothing in the world connects the trip to 'too many things on one strip'. The kettle and heater just look switched off. The wall gauge is tiny and floats in the doorway (see the gauge finding). The only way to learn the fix is to wander within 1.3 m of the kettle and read 'E Unplug the kettle', which is the text naming the method.
A new player will either loop on reset or think the projector is broken. This breaks DR-28 (failure shows its cause in the world, then one sentence naming the physical cause), DR-42 (card and marker point at the current step's object, not the projector) and DR-37 (hidden rule). It also weakens DR-26, because the lesson ends up taught by a prompt rather than by the scene.
evidence: src/meeting-strip.ts:63-66 (E within 1.6 m of the strip resets first; the appliance is found by find(), not nearest)
src/ui/objectives.ts:35 (step 3 text and at=switchAt, unchanged while tripped)
s3 log: 'reset no unplug … trips:2', 'reset again … trips:3', 'trips:4'
findings.fix:
(a) In src/ui/objectives.ts meeting step 3, make the text and marker state-aware: while g.strip?.tripped, show 'The power strip tripped: too much on it' (cause, not method) and set at() to the strip position. On the second trip, move the marker to the appliance drawing most (the kettle).
(b) In src/meeting-strip.ts render(), while tripped, float a small icon over each load still plugged into the strip (kettle, heater, projector). The icon is a stacked bar of its draw (2.5 / 2 / 1) next to a red limit line at 5, using the same Gauge zone colours. The sum then reads visually as 5.5 > 5.
(c) Make the reset refuse with a visible reason when it would instantly re-trip. If the load after reset exceeds STRIP_LIMIT, still trip (truthful), but on trips≥2 play a double-buzz, flash the overloaded zone on the gauge, and jiggle the kettle and heater cords.
(d) Have the kettle and heater keep a dim 'standby' LED (red dot) while tripped, so they read as 'plugged in, no power' rather than 'off'.
findings.verify: Rerun s3.mjs. After 'trip1', the card must change to the tripped text and the marker must sit over the strip (or the kettle after trip 2), and the per-load bars must be visible in shot 39 at the game camera. Add a test to tests/routes.spec.ts: switch on, expect the .objective .cur text to contain 'tripped', press E twice at the strip, and expect a marker world position within 1.5 m of the kettle.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced in v1.mjs. After the switch, strip.tripped is true and trips is 1. The card still says 'Switch the projector on in the boardroom' and the prompt is 'E Reset the strip'. Two more E presses took trips to 2 and then 3, with no change to the card or the prompt. The switch at (12.3, -3.2) is 1.25 m from the strip (under the 1.6 m in meeting-strip.ts:63), so pressing E at the switch resets the strip and re-trips it at once. objectives.ts:35 is step 3 with at=switchAt and no tripped state. Shot 07 shows a gold cable and a dark kettle and heater, with nothing tying the trip to the load. Fix (d) is electrically wrong, though. A kettle on a strip whose breaker has tripped has no supply, so a lit standby LED on it would break AGENTS 10.
extra_evidence: v1 log: trip → trips:1; 'E again' → trips:2; 'E again' → trips:3; prompt 'E Reset the strip' throughout
src/meeting-strip.ts:63 (reset branch comes before the appliance branch and has a 1.6 m radius that covers the switch spot)
findings.fix_correction: Keep (a) to (c). Replace (d): do not light anything on the unpowered kettle or heater. Show that they are still plugged in, but unpowered, through things that need no power. Their cords stay drawn into the strip (they already are), the strip's mechanical reset button pops up (resetCap already does this), and the gauge needle drops to 0 and shows a tripped flag. Also shrink the reset radius, or prefer the switch when Pip is closer to it, so that E at the projector switch does not silently reset and re-trip the strip.

findings.title: Strip load gauge floats in mid-air in the boardroom doorway, is unreadable at the game camera, and its 'only when placed' visibility is defeated by freeze()
findings.problem:
The load gauge is mounted at (t.x+0.95, 1.55, t.z+0.06) = (13.25, 1.55, -2.19). That point is inside the open door gap of the boardroom glass front, which spans x 11–13.8 at z -2, so nothing is behind or under the gauge. Orbited side and back shots show a thin black slab hovering at head height in the doorway with no wall, post or stand (shots 75, 76, 77). From the front it hangs over the boardroom carpet between chairs (23).
At the default game camera the dial is about 45×30 px, and its needle and zones cannot be read (shots 20, 22, 78). Yet the code comment says 'A gauge on the wall above the strip shows its load the whole time', so it is meant to be the main cue for the load lesson.
The gauge group is added to game.decorRoot, which freeze() merges and strips of empty groups after construction. The per-frame `gaugeMount.visible=g.stripPlaced()` therefore does nothing, and the gauge is visible from frame 1, before the strip exists (shots 02, 07).
This breaks DR-72 (nothing floats; signs mounted 0.5–1 cm off a surface), DR-63 (gauges have housings and finished backs; the back is a bare black box), DR-47 (device state readable at the game camera) and DR-48 (readable size).
evidence: src/render/kit.ts:77-85 (freeze merges meshes and removes empty groups)
src/levels/decor.ts:144-146 (glass front segments 9.3–11 and 13.8–16.5; door gap 11–13.8)
findings.fix: Mount the gauge on the glass front's door post at x 13.8 (the DMETAL post at src/levels/decor.ts:146), on its -x face, facing the door and the camera (+z): position (13.72, 1.6, -1.93), ry 0. Alternatively, put it on a short floor stand (cyl .03 × 1.3 m pole with a round foot) at (13.3, 0, -1.6). Add a housing: an rbox bezel 0.05 m larger than the face, with an INK back plate. Raise the scale from 0.8 to 1.4, so the dial is about 80×55 px at the default camera. Parent it to game.root (not decorRoot) so the visibility toggle works, or drop the toggle and show an empty, unlit gauge until the strip is placed. Also put a mini 3-segment LED bar on the strip itself (green/yellow/red) so the load reads on the device.
findings.verify: Rerun s8.mjs: shots 75/76 must show the gauge attached to a post or stand, with a finished back. At the game camera (shot 78) the needle angle must be distinguishable between draw 0 and 4.5 A in a crop. In s1.mjs shot 02 (before the strip is placed) the gauge must be hidden or visibly unlit.
findings.verify_reason: In code, gauge.mount is called on decorRoot at (13.25, 1.55, -2.19) (meeting-strip.ts:52). That point is inside the door gap between the posts at x 11 and 13.8 (decor.ts:144-146). freeze(decorRoot) runs after MeetingStrip is built (game.ts:103 then 105). It merges the gauge's meshes and removes the now-empty group (kit.ts:83-84), so gaugeMount.visible at meeting-strip.ts:85 has no effect. My shot at 0:05, before the strip was fetched (stripPlaced false), shows the gauge already up, hanging in the doorway beside the boardroom chairs with nothing under it. At the default camera (shot 03) it is a dial about 40×25 px. The proposed fix is technically off: the door post at x 13.8 is a 0.1×0.1 m bar (decor.ts:146), and a dial 0.98 m wide at scale 1.4 cannot mount on it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-meeting-play-20-door-before-strip-close.jpg (gauge visible at 0:05, step 1, no strip placed)
findings.fix_correction: Mount the gauge on a surface that exists. Either back it with a board on the boardroom glass segment east of the door, for example centred at (14.6, 1.6, -1.95) on the +z face of the glass at z -2, above the kettle table and facing the door and camera; or put it on a floor stand at about (13.3, 0, -1.6). Do not use the 0.1 m door post. Keep the rest: bezel and back plate, scale about 1.4, parent to game.root (not decorRoot) so the visibility toggle works, and an LED bar on the strip.

findings.title: The star cable shows no current pulses while it feeds the kettle and heater (4.5 A), and stays 'live gold' while the breaker is tripped
findings.problem:
Once the server cable is plugged into the strip, the kettle steams and the heater grille glows: the cable is carrying 4.5 A (snapshot draw 4.5). The cable turns gold but shows no moving pulses (shots 18, 19), because Pulses.update is gated on loads[0], the projector, alone. Pulses appear only after the win, when the projector runs.
After a trip, nothing flows (draw 0), yet the cable stays the same 'connected' gold (shots 22, 39). The tint is keyed to `connected`, not to current.
In the one room that teaches 'loads on a strip add up', the cable says the opposite: it shows the kettle and heater taking no current, and shows a tripped circuit as still live. This breaks DR-29 (moving dots mean current flows and only then), DR-46 ('a live cable carries pulses') and DR-47 (state shown on the device). It also weakens AGENTS 10 (truthful at the level taught).
evidence: src/game.ts:305 (pulses on only when circuit.loads[0].state==='on', i.e. the projector)
s2 log: plugged → draw 4.5, kettle/heater on, electrical off
findings.fix: In src/game.ts drawCable(), compute live = (this.circuit.draw.get('supply')??0) > 0 && !this.circuit.sources[0].tripped. Pass live to pulses.update instead of loads[0].state==='on'. Keep pulse speed constant (DR-30) and scale pulse density or brightness with draw/STRIP_LIMIT, so 4.5 A looks busier than 1 A. Tint the hose GOLD only while live; when connected but tripped, use a desaturated grey-gold (#b9ad86) and stop the pulses.
findings.verify: Rerun s2.mjs. Shot 19 (plugged, projector off) must show pulses along the gold cable, and shots 22/39 (tripped) must show a dull cable with no pulses. Add a unit check: after plugging in the meeting, snapshot a pulses 'on' flag (expose it in snapshot) and expect true while draw>0.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:305 passes circuit.loads[0].state==='on' (the projector) to Pulses.update, and actors.ts:84 hides the slugs whenever that flag is false. The tint at game.ts:304 is keyed only to this.connected. In v1, after plugging in, the snapshot shows draw 4.5 with the kettle and heater on, and shot 06 shows a gold cable with no cyan slugs while the kettle steams and the heater glows. After the trip (draw 0), shot 07 still shows the same gold cable.
extra_evidence: v1 log: plugged → draw 4.5, kettle/heater on

findings.title: Coupler-before-reel rule is still hidden: carrying the reel to the plug silently does nothing, the coupler hides behind the reel, and the plug Pip holds is itself a coupler model
findings.problem:
The clean route needs the coupler fitted before the second reel. In blind play:
(1) The obvious move is to grab the big yellow reel off the mail cart and carry it to the server plug. Pressing E there just drops it: no buzz, no wobble, no badge (couplerHint stays false; s3 log 'after E reel {max:23.2}'). The dropped reel also interpenetrates the anchor reel, which has no collider (shot 32). The wrong-order buzz only exists in attachNear, which needs the player to hold the plug.
(2) The coupler is a small teal block (0.36×0.24 m) on the cart, behind the reel and mostly hidden by it (shots 30, 79). Its shape does not say 'joins two cables'.
(3) The plug in Pip's hand is built with makeProp('coupler','#ffcc52'), the same prefab in yellow, so the prompt 'F Attach the coupler first' (shot 33) refers to an object identical to the one the player is holding.
(4) The coupler badge that appears after a wrong try floats over the coupler at the mail cart, 13 m away and off-screen while the player stands at the closet (shot 34).
R4B M8 asked that the order explain itself physically; this is still PARTIAL. It breaks DR-37 (order constraints show in the shape of the parts), DR-17 (false affordance: the plug looks like the coupler) and DR-50 (one name and look per thing).
evidence: src/game.ts:207 (carried extension near plug only works if this.coupler, else nothing)
src/game.ts:232-239 (wrong-order buzz only in attachNear while holding the plug)
src/levels/meeting.ts:27 (coupler at -3.6,4.7,y .9 next to reel at -3,4.7,y 1)
findings.fix:
(a) Use the existing 'plug' prefab kind (src/props/prefabs.ts PropKind includes 'plug') for this.plug, so the hand-held end reads as a male plug.
(b) Model the coupler as a distinct double-ended socket adapter (two female faces, a bright band), sitting on top of the reel drum (y 1.38, in the reel's hub) so it is the first thing seen on the cart, not behind it.
(c) Give the second reel's free end a visible female socket that clearly does not match the plug (an ink-blue face with slot holes), so the mismatch is readable before trying.
(d) In game.ts interact(), when the held extension is dropped within 2 m of plugPosition and !this.coupler, run the same wobble and buzz as attachNear, set couplerHint=true, and float the badge over the reel as well as the coupler.
(e) Add a solid() collider for the anchor reel at (level.anchor) in game.ts so dropped parts don't sink into it.
findings.verify: Rerun s3.mjs. After 'at plug with reel', pressing E must log couplerHint true and show a badge in shot 32 next to Pip. Shot 79 must show the coupler on top of the reel, and shot 12 must show a plug that differs from the coupler. Add a test to tests/routes.spec.ts: carry the extension to the plug first, press E, and expect snapshot couplerHint===true (expose it).
findings.verify_reason: Each sub-claim checks out in code, and the key shots match. (1) game.ts:207: a held extension near the plug only does anything when this.coupler is set. Otherwise it falls through to a plain drop with no buzz and no couplerHint; the buzz exists only in attachNear (game.ts:232-239), which needs the plug in hand. Shot 32 shows the dropped reel sitting in the anchor reel, which is built as a visual group with no collider (game.ts:90-91). (2) Shot 79 shows the coupler as a small teal block half hidden behind the big reel on the cart. (3) game.ts:86 builds the hand-held plug with makeProp('coupler','#ffcc52'), while a separate 'plug' PropKind exists (prefabs.ts:25). (4) The badge is placed over the coupler (meeting-strip.ts:87), which is about 14.7 m from the anchor.
findings.fix_correction: (b) Sitting the coupler on top of the round reel drum is unstable, because both are dynamic props and it will roll off. Put it in a tray or bin on the cart deck in front of the reel instead, or make it a fixed child of the cart until it is picked up. The rest stands.

findings.title: Grading is always A: sprint chaos 0:29, clean coupler route 0:39, and a 14-break wreck run all grade A on the 120 s / 10 / 300 defaults
findings.problem:
Big Meeting calls grade() with no limits, so it gets the cable-floor default of 120 s / 10 damage / 300 cost, with the overall grade the best of three.
- The sprint-overstretch chaos run finished in 0:29 with 0 damage: A/A/A (shot 28).
- The clean coupler route finished in 0:39: A/A/A (shot 40).
- An aisle sprint at overstretch broke 14 things and cost 245 in 6 seconds (shot 68). That scores damage B but time A, so the overall is still A.
There is no grade reason ever to learn the coupler route, which is the 'clean solution' and the room's routing lesson. It is slower than chaos and never cheaper. Players will learn that the deadline (4:00) and the limits don't matter. This breaks DR-07 (each axis tuned per room; standing still or wrecking can't earn A on all three) and AGENTS 6. The result card also gives the A without showing which axis earned it.
evidence: src/game.ts:354 (grade(this.time,this.damage,this.cost,this.station?.limits): no limits for cable floors)
findings.fix:
Add an optional limits field to Level (src/levels/types.ts) and pass level.limits in game.ts win(). For the meeting, time 60 s (the clean route at walking pace is about 45–55 s; the drive-script sprint route is 29–39 s), damage 3 and cost 80. Then a tidy coupler run gets A on damage and cost, a chaos sprint gets A on time but loses damage when it drags chairs, and a wreck gets an A only on time.
Consider grading on the median axis rather than the best, or show all three letters with the best highlighted and its axis named ('A: Speed').
On the result card, label which bar produced the headline grade.
findings.verify: Rerun s2.mjs, s3.mjs and the s7 aisle-sprint run: the result cards must differ (the wreck run's headline must be named as coming from time only, and its damage bar must show C or D). Extend tests/routes.spec.ts so each meeting route asserts the grade parts it is expected to earn.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:354 calls grade() with only this.station?.limits, so cable floors get the 120/10/300 defaults. grade.ts:6 sets overall = best part. My sprint run graded A/A/A at 0:29 with 0 damage (result card). Under the same rule, 14 damage and 245 cost ranks B and A on those axes and A on time, so the overall is A. The proposed limits do not fix this, though. The sprint-overstretch run had 0 damage and 0 cost (my v1 run), so with 60/3/80 it is still A/A/A and still faster than the coupler route. The best-of-three rule also still lets a wreck earn an A overall.
findings.fix_correction: Per-room limits are necessary but not enough. Change the overall from best-of-three to the median (or the mean rank), so a wreck that is A only on time cannot headline an A. Calibrate limits.time from walking-pace runs, not from drive.walkTo, which auto-sprints beyond 2.5 m (game.ts:473); a 60 s limit would grade honest first runs C. If the sprint overstretch is meant as the chaos shortcut, give it a cost: for example, pulling at strain > 1.0 for more than 0.5 s scuffs the cable sheath (+1 damage, +20 cost). Then it trades grade for speed instead of strictly dominating the coupler route.

findings.title: R restarts the job instantly, with no confirm, on a key next to E, F and Q
findings.problem: During play, KeyR calls action('restart'), which does location.reload() at once. In s4 I pressed R at 43.4 s into a run and the job reloaded at 0:00 with no prompt (shot 45). R sits between E and T and right above F on QWERTY, and E/F/Q are the three most-pressed keys in this room. A missed E or F press at the end of a 2-minute run (for example at the strip or the switch) wipes all progress. Big Meeting's runs are the longest cable runs (37 m of cable and several back-and-forth trips), so the cost of a slip is highest here. This breaks DR-19 (a key never undoes what the player is trying to do) and DR-22 (consistent, safe controls). Instant retry belongs on the fail and result cards, not in the middle of play.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts setupInput, while running && !paused && !won, require R to be held for 0.8 s. Show a small radial fill on the pause button and cancel on release. Alternatively, make R during play open the pause menu with Restart focused. Keep instant R on the result, fail and pause screens (game-ui.ts:119 already distinguishes screens).
findings.verify: Script: press and release R quickly mid-run, then expect snapshot().time > 0 and the same level state. Hold R for 0.9 s (keyboard.down, then wait, then up), then expect a reload. Add this to tests/objectives.spec.ts.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:166 sends KeyR to action('restart') whenever running && !won, and game.ts:178 calls location.reload() with no confirmation; game-ui.ts:119 also sets the autostart flag. In v3, pressing R at t=2.8 s reloaded straight into play at t 0, with Pip back at the spawn (-10, -5.8).

findings.title: Phone survey (Tab) at 390×844 shows only the middle third of the office: closet, boardroom, lounge and coffee corner are cut off
findings.problem: The survey uses a fixed zoom of 44 with the room centre as its target. On the portrait phone viewport (390×844) the frame covers only the central desk pods (shot 47). The server closet (the reel), the boardroom and strip door (the goal), the coffee corner (the sneaky reel) and the lounge are all outside the frame. Survey is the only way to see the whole job on a phone, so a phone player can't see where the job starts or ends. At 1440×900 the same survey shows the whole room (shot 02), so this is an aspect problem. QA 7 (survey crops the vending side and lounge) was claimed fixed, but only for landscape. This breaks DR-21 (the survey shows the whole room, with every wall and the goal, at 16:10 and on a phone in portrait).
findings.fix: In updateCamera, compute the survey distance from the room bounds and the camera aspect. From horizontal FOV hfov = 2*atan(tan(fov/2)*aspect), dist = max((level.width/2+1)/tan(hfov/2), (level.depth/2+1)/tan(fov/2)) / cos(pitch) * 1.05. In portrait (aspect<1), also rotate the survey yaw by π/2, so the 33 m long axis runs up the screen; that roughly halves the distance needed. Restore the yaw when leaving the survey.
findings.verify: Rerun s4.mjs phone section. Shot 47 must show the closet reel, the boardroom door and the lounge, with all four room edges visible. Add a portrait check: project the four floor corners in survey mode and expect all inside NDC ±1.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced at 390×844. After Tab, the frame shows only the central desk pods and the mail cart. The server closet, the boardroom and strip door, the coffee corner and the lounge are all off-screen. game.ts:366 uses a fixed zoom of 44 around the room centre, whatever the aspect ratio. At 1440×900 the same survey shows the whole floor.

findings.title: Coworkers have no colliders: Pip walks straight through blobs and thrown props pass through them
findings.problem:
addNpc builds coworkers as plain THREE groups with no Rapier body. Pip can stand inside a standing coworker: shot 85 shows the green coffee-corner blob's body wrapped around Pip's legs. Thrown props and slingshotted chairs fly through coworkers instead of bonking them.
In a physics-comedy office with 24 coworkers this throws away the cheapest slapstick there is (bumping a coworker, knocking a mug off a blob's head). It also looks broken: an interpenetration the player causes all the time on the dense desk aisles. The audit (game.ts audit) treats coworkers as 0.36 m balls for start overlap only, so the design already assumes they are solid.
This breaks DR-70 (nothing interpenetrates) and DR-04 (the world reacts to chaos). It also undercuts DR-03 (something funny happens in the first 30 s without looking for it).
findings.fix: In addNpc, create a fixed (or kinematicPositionBased) Rapier body with a capsule collider: half-height 0.3, radius 0.34, centred at y 0.65 (seated: y 1.0, radius 0.3). Register the collider handle on the Npc. In step(), use world contact events, or a cheap per-frame check of dynamic props within 0.6 m of each npc whose speed is above 2.5 m/s, to call this.alarm(npc.position, 1.2) and give the npc a 0.25 s squash-wobble. Pip bumping a blob at a sprint triggers the same. Coworkers should not count as damage.
findings.verify: Rerun s10.mjs: walk toward (-12.7, 2.8). Pip must stop at about 0.7 m from the blob centre (arrived false), and shot 85 must show no overlap. Rerun s9.mjs: the thrown bin must bounce off the blue coworker, with alarmed ≥1 from that contact.
findings.verify_reason: addNpc (game.ts:127-135) builds only THREE groups, with no Rapier body. In v2, walkTo(-12.7, 2.8) reported arrived:true with Pip at (-12.54, 2.71), 0.18 m from the standing coworker's centre. The close-up shows the green blob wrapped around Pip's legs. The audit puts a 0.36 m ball on standing coworkers only (game.ts:497-499, not 488-489 as cited). The proposed fix would cause new overlaps, though. Seated coworkers are spawned at exactly the chair positions (meeting.ts:15,18 use chairX and z+out for both the chair and the npc), so a fixed capsule at every coworker would overlap the dynamic chairs and pop them at start, breaking DR-70.
extra_evidence: v2 log: 'walk into coworker arrived true {x:-12.54,z:2.71}'
src/levels/meeting.ts:15,18 (seated npc shares the chair's x,z)
findings.fix_correction: Give the 2 standing coworkers a kinematic capsule (radius .34, half-height .3, centre y .65). For seated coworkers, do not add a separate body at the chair position. Either attach the blob's collider to the chair's own rigid body (as an extra collider), or use a sensor that only triggers the bonk and wobble and the alarm, so the chairs are not ejected. Rerun g.audit(0.02) and expect no new overlaps.

findings.title: Prompt and card disagree at three moments: start ('Pick up the plug'), after placing the strip ('Grab the power strip'), and at the heater ('Unplug the kettle')
findings.problem:
(1) Start, a known issue confirmed. The card says 'Fetch the power strip by the printer and set it at the boardroom door', while the key prompt says 'F Pick up the plug', because Pip spawns 1 m from the reel plug (shots 01, 46). A new player's very first instruction from the two allowed text lines is contradictory, and following the prompt starts dragging the cable before the strip exists.
(2) After the strip snaps in, standing at it the prompt reads 'E Grab the power strip' (shots 75, 78) while the card says 'Bring the server-room cable…'. The prompt offers to undo step 1, because the placed strip (now a Fixed body) is still in nearest() with job-item priority.
(3) At the appliances, appliance choice uses find(), not nearest. At (15, -0.9), 0.4 m from the heater, the prompt still says 'Unplug the kettle' (shot 77, s3 log), so the player can't target the heater from in front of it.
This breaks DR-42 (the prompt points at the current step's object), DR-18 (selection prefers the right item) and DR-19 (every prompt is the real useful action at that moment).
evidence: src/ui/objectives.ts:81 ('Pick up the plug' regardless of step)
findings.fix:
(a) In promptFor, when the current step is not the cable step (the meeting needs the strip and g.needsStrip() && !g.stripPlaced()), skip the 'Pick up the plug' line unless the plug is within 0.9 m and in front of Pip. Instead, when the strip is out of reach, return the nearest-job-item prompt or null.
(b) In Game.nearest(), exclude props whose body is Fixed (the placed strip) unless the player is holding nothing and the current step is 1, or exclude the strip entirely once stripPlaced().
(c) In MeetingStrip.interact/prompt, pick the appliance with the minimum dist(pos, x.at) among those within 1.3 m.
(d) Spawn Pip at (-9.6, -4.9), facing the printer, so the strip, not the plug, is the nearest interactable at frame 1.
findings.verify: Rerun s1.mjs: shot 01's prompt must name the power strip or nothing. In s8.mjs, shot 75 must not show 'Grab the power strip', and at (15, -0.9) the prompt must read 'Unplug the heater'. Extend tests/objectives.spec.ts 'Big Meeting shows the power-strip step' to assert that the start prompt does not contain 'plug'.
findings.verify_reason: All three moments reproduced. (1) v1 start: the card says to fetch the strip while the prompt says 'F Pick up the plug'; the spawn (-10, -5.8) is 1.48 m from the plug at anchor+0.7, under the 1.75 m in objectives.ts:81. (2) In v2, after placing the strip, the prompt read 'E Grab the power strip' at all four positions I tried around the door (11.0,-1.4), (12.1,-1.15), (12.7,-1.0) and (11.9,-1.5). (3) At (14.91, -1.01), 0.71 m from the heater and 1.13 m from the kettle, the prompt read 'E Unplug the kettle', because meeting-strip.ts:66,75 uses find() over a list with the kettle first. It only switched to the heater at (15.22, -1.07).
extra_evidence: v2 log: 'heater try 14.91 -1.01 … E Unplug the kettle'; 'at 12.3 -1.1 … E Grab the power strip'

findings.title: The sprint-overstretch chaos route is undiscoverable: at the walking stall the prompt says 'Q Let go to slingshot', which throws the plug away, instead of hinting that sprinting stretches further
findings.problem:
Walking with the single 23.2 m reel, Pip stalls at x≈10.0, z -1.6 with strain 1.02. That is 1.73 m from the snap zone, which needs <1.6 (shots 15, 16), so the target ring is right there. The only prompt is 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable'. Doing that (or pressing F, which also calls releasePlug) flings the plug back toward the last bend, wasting the walk.
Nothing in the world or HUD suggests holding Shift. Sprinting is the secret that gets the extra 0.4 m and makes the 'Plug in' prompt appear (shot 17, strain 1.04). This is the room's best chaos beat: the cable goes red, coworkers duck with '!' bubbles, chairs drag (shots 17, 68). Most players will never find it, or will find it only by accident. R4B M9 is still PARTIAL.
This breaks DR-37 (range tricks such as sprinting to overstretch get a visible hint) and DR-06 (the slingshot is discoverable, with a reward in reach). It also undermines DR-01, which needs the chaos route to be playable, not just scripted.
evidence: src/ui/objectives.ts:79 (strain>.97 → 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable')
tests/routes.spec.ts 'meeting single reel only reaches when overstretched at a sprint' (drives advance(['KeyD','ShiftLeft']))
s2 log: walk D strain 1.02 pos 10.0; sprint strain 1.04 pos 10.4 → 'F Plug in'
findings.fix: In promptFor, when holdingPlug && strain>0.97 && !g.extension && dist(plug, target) < 4, return {key:'Shift', text:'Sprint to stretch it'} (the action bar already has the slot style for keys). Otherwise keep the slingshot prompt. In drawCable, add a visual: when stalled at a strain of 0.97–1.05 and not sprinting, pulse the hose's last metre and puff dust at Pip's feet as the boots skid (Pip leaning forward in the rig). Optionally widen the forgiving snap for the overstretched cable to 1.8 m, so a walking player who presses F gets a 'so close' wobble rather than a slingshot.
findings.verify: Rerun s2.mjs. At 'walk D strain 1.02' the prompt must name Shift/sprint (shot 15). Add a test to tests/objectives.spec.ts: at the stall, expect .prompt-pill to contain 'Sprint'.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced exactly. Walking with D stalls at x 10.12, z -1.58 at strain 1.02, with the prompt 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable'. Sprinting for 1.5 s reaches x 10.44 at strain 1.04 and the prompt becomes 'F Plug in' (objectives.ts:78-79, game.ts:205). F outside the snap zone calls releasePlug (game.ts:205, else branch). The proposed fix conflicts with the project's own text rule, though. The objectives code says hints are 'Goals, not methods' (objectives.ts:47), and AGENTS asks for play by doing, so a prompt that names the trick ('Sprint to stretch it') is a method in text.
extra_evidence: v1 log: 'walk stall strain 1.02 pos 10.12 -1.58 … Q Let go to slingshot'; 'sprint strain 1.04 pos 10.44 … F Plug in'
findings.fix_correction: Lead with world cues, not text. At a walking stall within 4 m of the target, Pip leans into the pull with skidding boots and dust, the plug end strains toward the ring, and the ring pulses. Pressing F there gives a 'so close' wobble (with the snap distance widened to about 1.8 m for the feedback check) instead of releasing the plug. Show a Shift key glyph on the sprint slot of the action bar only after a failed F at the stall, rather than as a sentence in the prompt pill.

findings.title: Letting go has no payoff in Meeting, and none of the three bonuses rewards chaos
findings.problem:
In s7 I sprinted the plug along the back aisle to overstretch (strain 1.04), dragging chairs (14 breaks during the drag; a chair flew out of the pod, shot 68), then pressed Q. On release the plug only moves 15% toward the last bend and drops. Props 1.5 s later move at under 2.7 m/s, nothing visibly launches (shots 69–71), and alarmed fell to 0. The slingshot, which AGENTS 4 calls a signature of the cable and which the Playground rewards with six pins and a confetti strike, has no target here: no fling target is set up on any plausible route.
All three meeting bonuses are tidy: finish before 4:00, break fewer than 5, leave the coffee machine alone. A chaos player has nothing to chase, and the room actively penalises the fun stuff through the star HUD (a star greyed after breaking). The funniest moments (coworkers ducking with '!' bubbles as the red cable whips past, shot 17) are incidental.
This breaks DR-06 (a fling target within reel length + 2 m), DR-10 (at least one physical or chaos bonus, visible in the survey) and AGENTS 5 (chaos rewarded, never punished).
evidence: src/game.ts:255-258 (slingshot impulses only props within 1.1 m of the rope)
src/game.ts:260-264 (releasePlug: plug lerps .15 toward the last bend)
findings.fix:
(a) Add a fling target in reach of the sprint route. One option is a 'paper tower': a 3×3×2 pyramid of 'box' props, ids tower-*, at the aisle end (7.8, -0.4), within reel length + 2 m of the plug's natural route and visible in the survey. Score a 'topple' like pinsDown (tipped or moved >0.5 m), with a confetti burst and jingle at all down.
(b) Replace one tidy bonus with a chaos bonus, e.g. 'Topple the paper tower', or 'Make 10 coworkers duck at once' (alarmed≥10 in one frame), keeping 'Finish before 4:00' and 'Leave the coffee machine alone'. Tower boxes must not count as damage.
(c) Make releasePlug snap harder: lerp 0.45 toward the last bend, and have slingshot() also impulse the 3 nearest props at the bend with min(energy*.3, 45).
findings.verify: Rerun s7.mjs: after Q, at least one tower-* prop must move >1 m (snapshot items), with a confetti burst in shot 70. The pause/result card must list a chaos bonus. Add a test 'meeting slingshot topples the paper tower' to tests/routes.spec.ts.
findings.verify_reason: In code, the three meeting bonuses at objectives.ts:36-39 are all tidy (time, damage below 5, coffee machine untouched), and nothing in meeting.ts is a fling target. Playground has pins and a strike cheer (game.ts:347); the meeting has none. releasePlug only lerps the plug 0.15 toward the last bend (game.ts:262). The reviewer's aftermath shot (14 breaks, cost 245 at 0:07) shows the plug just lying in the aisle, with no launched props or payoff visible. I did not re-measure the prop speeds after release myself.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:347 (only playground has a chaos-target cheer)

findings.title: Backtracking: the strip-first order sends Pip across the same aisle five times on the clean route; most of the run is walking
findings.problem:
The strip starts by the printer, 2 m from the reel, but must be set at the boardroom door, 21 m away. The cable can't be dragged while carrying it. So every route is: carry the strip 21 m east, walk back 22 m west, then drag the cable 25 m east again. The clean coupler route adds closet→cart→closet (2×13 m), or cart and back twice if the parts are carried separately as the spec does.
In the drive script (which auto-sprints whenever the target is more than 2.5 m away) the strip was placed at 9.6 s, I was back at the reel at 10.1 s, and the clean route finished at 39 s, of which roughly 120 m was traversal. At normal walking speed (4.2 m/s) that is about 29 s of pure walking in a 45–55 s job. Each leg passes the same desks, and nothing new happens on the return trip. It isn't a soft-lock, but it is the kind of dead time DR-09 targets ('no walk longer than 8 s passes nothing interactive'), and it makes the room feel like a fetch quest before the fun starts.
evidence: src/levels/meeting.ts:26 (strip at -8.6,-3.2 next to the reel)
s1/s3 logs: strip placed 9.6 s, back at reel 10.1 s, clean finish 39.3 s
findings.fix: Let the strip ride on the cable: with the strip held, pressing F next to the plug (or picking up the plug next to a dropped strip) plugs the reel into the strip, and Pip then carries the strip as the plug end. Setting it down within 2.6 m of the door completes both step 1 and step 2. That keeps the order (strip, then cable) and halves the walking. Alternatively, start the strip in the lounge (12.5, 4.2) under the lounge desk, so it is a 6 m detour at the far end, and reorder the card ('Bring the cable to the boardroom door', then 'The strip there is missing: find one'). If either is done, retune limits.time (see the grading finding).
findings.verify: Rerun s3.mjs with the new interaction and log the time at won: the clean route should drop by at least 8 s. Update tests/routes.spec.ts placeStrip/backToReel and the clean-route test to the new flow.
findings.verify_reason: meeting.ts:26 puts the strip at (-8.6, -3.2), and the target is (12.3, -2.25), 20.9 m apart. The anchor (-11.4, -7.8) is next to the strip, so every route goes strip east, walk back west, then drag the cable east. In my v1 run (auto-sprinting), the strip was placed at 8.0 s and the win came at 29.8 s, so most of the run is traversal. At the 4.2 m/s walking speed (game.ts:318), the strip leg alone is about 5 s each way.
extra_evidence: v1 log: 'strip placed true t 8.0' … 'won true t 29.8'

findings.title: Borrowing the coffee reel after the server cable is plugged in leaves the strip live with nothing connected
findings.problem: In s6 run C: I plugged the server cable into the strip (kettle and heater on, draw 4.5), then walked to the coffee corner and pressed E on the coffee reel. The rope reset to the coffee machine's 30 m cable in Pip's hand, the server cable vanished from the floor (shot 65), and holdingPlug became true. But `connected` stayed true, so circuit.leads[0].closed stayed true. The strip kept feeding the kettle and heater (draw 4.5) while its only cable was in Pip's hand at the far end of the office. At the switch, the projector could have been run from a strip connected to nothing. It is an edge case, but it is a direct electrical falsehood, and AGENTS 10 is a hard rule. It also looks odd: the server cable teleports away.
evidence: src/game.ts:222 (coffee-reel branch resets rope and sets holdingPlug, does not clear connected)
s6 log C: 'after coffee {hp:true, draw:4.5, …kettle on, heater on}'
findings.fix: In the coffee-reel branch of Game.interact (src/game.ts:222), add `this.connected=false; this.circuit.leads[0].closed=false;` before the rope reset. Better still, refuse to borrow the coffee reel while the server cable is plugged in: shrug and show the prompt 'Unplug your cable first'. Also play a short retract animation of the server cable back to its spool instead of an instant vanish.
findings.verify: Rerun s6.mjs part C: 'after coffee' must log draw 0 and kettle/heater off (or the borrow must be refused). Add a unit-style test in tests/routes.spec.ts: connect, borrow the coffee reel, and expect snapshot().strip.draw===0.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced in v3. I connected the server cable (draw 4.5, kettle and heater on), then pressed E on the coffee reel. Afterwards holdingPlug is true and the rope is reset to 1.56 m at the coffee machine, but the strip still reports draw 4.5 with the kettle and heater on. The survey shot shows no server cable on the floor while the kettle keeps steaming. game.ts:222 never clears this.connected, and game.ts:348 keeps leads[0].closed = connected && stripPlaced. A player could then drop the coffee plug and run the projector from a strip with no cable connected.
extra_evidence: v3 log: 'after coffee {hp:true, strip:{draw:4.5, kettle on, heater on}, rope:1.56}'

findings.title: Placed power strip is buried under the Playground's black 'socket' box, and the cyan target ring stays after plug-in
findings.problem: game.ts always builds a 0.48×0.38×0.3 dark socket box at level.target for every cable floor, and hides it only in stations and the lobby. In the meeting the strip snaps to (t.x, 0.08, t.z+0.3). The socket box at (t.x, 0.25, t.z) then sits on top of the strip, covering most of its sockets; only the red reset button and one corner of the orange strip show (shots 23, 75, 77). The player places a strip and then sees a black block where the strip should be. Once the cable is plugged in, the cyan torus target ring keeps pulsing around the strip, so the 'done' state looks like the 'go here' state. This breaks DR-70 (nothing interpenetrates at rest) and makes DR-47 (device state on the device) worse, because the strip's own sockets and the plugs in them are hidden.
evidence: src/game.ts:87-88 (target torus and socket box at level.target)
findings.fix: In the Game constructor, set socket.visible=false when level.id==='meeting' (the strip is the socket there). In render(), hide this.target once this.connected, or scale it to 0 over 0.3 s on plug-in. Draw the plugged plug on the strip's first socket: plugPosition = strip top socket (t.x-0.3, 0.17, t.z+0.3).
findings.verify: Rerun s8.mjs shot 75 and s2 shot 23: the orange strip with four sockets must be fully visible, with the plug in its first socket and no black block, and the cyan ring must be gone after 'plugged'.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:88 always builds the dark 0.48×0.38×0.3 socket box at the target, and it hides it only for stations and the hub (game.ts:92). The strip snaps to (t.x, .08, t.z+.3) (game.ts:211), so the box sits over most of it. My close-up shows a black block on the orange strip, with only the strip's edge showing. After plug-in, the cyan torus is still there and still pulsing (game.ts:431 scales it every frame, and nothing hides it).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-meeting-play-06-plugged-cable.jpg (ring still around the strip after plug-in)

findings.title: Grab prompts fall back to 'Grab the thing' for the vending machine and the boardroom glass panes
findings.problem: NAMES in objectives.ts has no entry for vending, glass, coffee or pingpong. Walking up to the vending machine in the coffee corner shows 'E Grab the thing (heavy: push it)' (sheet shots 53–56). At the boardroom's west glass panes it shows 'E Grab the thing' (shot 72). The panes carry ids (glass-0..2), so they win the job-item reach priority over everything else near the boardroom, and this fallback is the prompt a player is most likely to see there. It reads as unfinished and gives no clue that the panes are the 'smash the glass' chaos shortcut. This breaks DR-50 (one name per thing; 'Grab the thing' fallbacks are a known fail).
findings.fix: Add to NAMES: vending:'vending machine', glass:'glass panel', coffee:'coffee machine', pingpong:'ping-pong table', and any other PropKind used in meeting.ts. Make the fallback the kind name with dashes removed, never 'thing'. Add a unit test that every PropKind in prefabs has a NAMES entry.
findings.verify: Rerun s5.mjs and s7.mjs: the vending prompt must read 'Grab the vending machine (heavy: push it)' and the glass prompt 'Grab the glass panel…'. Unit test over Object.keys(prefabs).
findings.verify_reason: NAMES (objectives.ts:57-59) has no entries for vending, glass, coffee, pingpong or plug, all of which are PropKinds (prefabs.ts:4). In v2, standing at (8.46, -3.33) by glass-2 gave 'E Grab the thing'. The reviewer's sheet shows 'Grab the thing (heavy: push it)' beside the vending machine. In my own vending test the nearer crates won, so the prompt read 'Grab the crate'.
extra_evidence: v2 log: 'by glass … E Grab the thing'

findings.title: The coffee machine's 'live cable' is a loose spare reel on the floor, identical to the server reel and the mail-cart reel
findings.problem: The sneaky route ('unplug the coffee machine's extension, which is live and fed from the closet', LEVEL_01) depends on the player noticing that the coffee machine runs on a reel they can borrow. In the build, the coffee reel is the same yellow reel prefab as the anchor reel and the mail-cart reel, lying on the floor at (-12.7, 4.5) (shots 85, 02). No cable runs from it to the coffee machine or the wall, so it reads as a third spare reel. Its only signposting is the text prompt 'Borrow the coffee machine's cable' when standing next to it. Three identical reels with three different rules is a false-affordance problem (DR-17), and the hidden wiring breaks DR-37 ('invisible wiring is drawn'). The groan payoff is good, but few players will find the route.
findings.fix: Draw the coffee machine's cord: a TubeGeometry from the machine's back (-14, 1.1, 5) down the counter leg to the coffee reel, and from the reel to a wall socket on the side wall (-16.3, 0.4, 4.5). Give the coffee reel a coffee-brown flange colour (#7a4f33) and a small mug decal so it reads as 'the coffee machine's'. When the cord is borrowed, retract it with the existing rope reset.
findings.verify: Survey shot 02 and close-up shot 85: a visible cord must connect the coffee machine, the reel and the wall, and the reel must differ in colour from the server reel.
findings.verify_reason: meeting.ts:28 places the coffee reel as a default 'reel' prop on the floor at (-12.7, 4.5), with nothing linking it to the coffee machine. In my close-up of the coffee corner, it is a yellow reel lying on the floor beside the purple coworker, with no cord to the machine or the wall. Its colours match the anchor reel and the mail-cart reel. The only cue is the prompt text at objectives.ts:82.

findings.title: No edge-of-screen indicator: after each step the marker jumps to a target 13–24 m away and off-screen
findings.problem: The objective marker is a world-space cone at y 2.1 over the step's at() point. After the strip snaps in at the boardroom door, the next target is the server plug at the closet, 24 m away and off-screen at the default camera (shot 08). After a wrong-order buzz at the closet, the coupler badge appears over the coupler at the mail cart, which is off-screen too (shot 34). With the camera following Pip at zoom 22–26, a player who doesn't remember the layout has no pointer at all. The cone also has no outline (MeshBasicMaterial with outlineParameters off), so in busy desk areas it is hard to pick out (shot 13). This breaks DR-13 (the current step's target is never hidden) and DR-44 (the marker reads at the game camera: outlined, two-tone).
findings.fix: In ObjectivesHUD.update(), project the marker position. When it is outside the frustum (|ndc.x|>0.92 or |ndc.y|>0.88 or behind the camera), show a DOM chevron chip clamped to the screen edge, pointing toward it, with the step icon. Give the cone an INK outline (enable outlineParameters) and a two-tone material (toon with an emissive top), and raise it to 2.4 m when Pip is within 2 m, so it doesn't sit on Pip's helmet (shot 04).
findings.verify: Rerun s1.mjs: shot 08 must show an edge chevron on the left pointing toward the closet. Unit-check the chip's visibility in tests/objectives.spec.ts after placeStrip.
findings.verify_reason: The marker is a world-space cone with outlines turned off (objectives.ts:97-98), and there is no screen-edge fallback anywhere in ObjectivesHUD.update (objectives.ts:117-118). Right after the strip snaps in, my shot shows no marker on screen: the next target, the plug at the closet, is off-frame to the left.

findings.title: The idle route hint (after 35 s) leads to the door even when the strip hasn't been fetched, and it uses glowing current-like beads
findings.problem: After 35 s without connecting, 40 cyan glowing beads flow from Pip to level.target along a detour path (shots 43, 44, 67). During step 1 (the strip not fetched, card saying 'Fetch the power strip by the printer'), the beads still lead to the boardroom door, away from the strip that is 1 m behind Pip. So the hint contradicts the card. They also look exactly like current pulses moving along an open circuit, the 'electricity flows to the device' misconception (DR-29, a known issue confirmed here).
findings.fix: Route the hint to the current step's at(g) (export a helper from objectives.ts, or have ObjectivesHUD set g.hintTarget). Replace the glowing spheres with flat, non-emissive floor chevrons or footprints in job yellow (#ffd84a), spaced 0.8 m and fading in sequence, so the hint never resembles current.
findings.verify: Rerun s4.mjs: shot 43 must show chevrons from Pip to the strip (step 1), not to the door, with no emissive beads. grep game.ts for the bead material and expect no MeshBasic glow.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:446 always routes the hint to this.level.target whenever time > 35 and !connected, whatever the current step. game.ts:101 uses emissive-looking cyan MeshBasic beads (#9ff3ea ×1.4), close in hue to the current pulses (#6fe9ff, actors.ts:81). The reviewer's 0:40 shot shows the dots flowing east during step 1. In that shot the strip had been knocked east, so the 'opposite direction' part depends on where the strip lies, but the code always targets the door.

findings.title: Draw calls: 1237 at the start view and 1422 in the survey, five times the 250 budget
findings.problem: snapshot().drawCalls measured 1237 at the start view and 1422 in the survey at 1440×900 with fullfx (s1 log). R3B measured 1064 for the meeting; it has grown since. Big Meeting is the densest cable floor (310 props, 24 coworkers, a live rope mesh, pulses and particles). At ~5× DR-24's ≤250 budget it is the most likely room to drop frames on a laptop iGPU. adaptQuality would then step bloom and AO down mid-run, changing the look during the drag. The host-GPU fps reads 60, but in ?manual mode fps isn't representative.
evidence: src/game.ts:127-135 (each coworker is a separate blob group: calm + startled meshes)
findings.fix: Profile with renderer.info per pass. Likely wins: (1) merge each coworker's calm and startled blobs into instanced meshes by colour (24×2 groups now); (2) batch NPC sprites (bubble, sweat) into one InstancedMesh, or hide them when inactive (they are already invisible, so check that they aren't drawn); (3) put the outline pass on merged decor only, and turn outlines off on tiny props (mugs, paper) at zoom >20; (4) merge the 18 cabinets plus 18 boxes on the back wall into decor if they are never moved, or keep them dynamic but share a material.
findings.verify: Rerun s1.mjs: snapshot().drawCalls ≤ 400 at start as a first step (≤250 target), and in the survey. Add a perf assertion to tools/perf.mjs output for the meeting.
findings.verify_reason: Measured in my v1 run at 1440×900 with fullfx: drawCalls was 1314 at the start view and 1215 in the survey, so the survey is not higher than the start view as the reviewer reported. Both are about 5× DR-24's ~250 (RULES.md:167). The R3B figure was 1064 (review3/REVIEW_B.md:25). One proposed lever is wrong: the back-wall cabinets and boxes are dynamic chaos props that batchProps already instances (game.ts:139-142), so merging them into decor would remove their physics for little gain.
findings.fix_correction: Drop lever (4): the cabinets and boxes are already instanced, and freezing them would remove props players can knock over. Profile first: renderer.info per pass (composer, outline, shadow) and the per-coworker meshes (26 groups, each with calm and startled blobs, a sweat sprite and a bubble sprite). The likely wins are instancing the blobs by colour, skipping shadow casting on small props, and skipping the outline on sub-0.3 m props.

findings.title: Shoving a boardroom glass pane at a sprint slides it into the room, lifted and unbroken, instead of shattering
findings.problem: LEVEL_01's chaos route says 'smash the glass wall (big cost) to shorten the route'. In s7, sprinting Pip into the west glass pane glass-2 at (9.3, -3.6) for 1.2 s pushed the pane 2.6 m east into the boardroom (x 11.9) and raised it to y 1.7 (resting tilted on chairs or the table). It didn't break (damage 0, cost 0), and Pip entered the boardroom through the gap (shot 73). Damage only counts on a 5.5 m/s impact followed by a sudden stop, which a shove never produces. So the intended 'smash' reads as a ghost pane sliding about with Pip seen through it. The direct anchor→door line crosses this pane at z≈-2.95, so it matters for the chaos route.
evidence: src/levels/meeting.ts:32 (3 dynamic glass panes, mass 7, size .12×2.6×2.5)
findings.fix: Make glass panes fixed until hit: create them as Fixed bodies. On contact with Pip at sprint speed (>5 m/s), any prop faster than 4 m/s, or the taut cable at strain>1, switch the pane to 'shatter': consume it, spawn a glass burst plus shard debris, count damage and cost 250, and alarm the boardroom. A walking push should only rattle the pane (a small wobble tween).
findings.verify: Rerun s7.mjs glass section. A sprint into glass-2 must log damage 1, cost 250 and the pane hidden, with a shatter burst in shot 73. A walking push must leave the pane in place.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced in v2. Sprinting east from (8.46, -3.33) into glass-2 for 1.2 s pushed the pane from x 9.30 to 11.22 (z -3.81) with damage 0 and cost 0, and Pip went on through to x 15.4 inside the boardroom. findings.title: Lounge beanbag uses the exact job-item yellow (#ffc94d)
findings.problem: The lounge beanbag at (10, 4.6) is coloured '#ffc94d'. That is the job-item yellow shared by the reels, the plug, the target marker family and the reel flanges. In the survey and lounge shots (02, 76) the yellow blob near the boardroom is the brightest job-coloured shape on that side of the room, near the goal, competing with the strip and the marker. Its rounded shape also reads more like a yellow coworker or a bun than a seat. This breaks DR-45 (no decorative clutter uses the job-item yellow).
findings.fix: Change it to a fabric colour more than 25 ΔE from #ffc94d, e.g. coral '#e07a4f' or teal '#3fa7a0' (avoiding the BLOBC hues). Add a check in a unit test that no non-id prop in meeting.ts has a colour within 25 ΔE of #ffc94d/#ffc629/#ffd84a.
findings.verify: Survey shot 02: the only job-yellow shapes must be the reels, the strip area and the marker. Unit test over meeting props.
findings.verify_reason: meeting.ts:29 gives the lounge beanbag the colour '#ffc94d', which is the DR-45 job-item yellow (RULES.md:284). My lounge shots show it as a bright yellow blob near the boardroom, next to a yellow lamp shade. The prefab default beanbag colour in prefabs.ts:26 is also '#ffc94d', so any beanbag without an explicit colour has the same problem.
findings.fix_correction: Also change the beanbag prefab's default colour in src/props/prefabs.ts:26 (for example to '#e07a4f'), not only the meeting instance.

notes.fun:
What works: the core cable drag in Big Meeting is genuinely fun. The cable goes visibly white → yellow → orange → red as it pays out across the office (shots 13, 14, 15, 17), the HUD length bar fills in step, and pushing past the limit at a sprint makes coworkers pop '!' bubbles and drags chairs out of the pods (shots 17, 68). That is exactly the Good Job slapstick the brief asks for. The plug-in and the trip have punchy audio and a shake. Unplugging the kettle makes the whole boardroom groan, and borrowing the coffee reel makes the coffee corner groan (shots 25, 65); both are good comedic beats, and the coffee one is the best 'sneaky' moment in the game. The deadline clock and the impatient boardroom after 4:00 are a nice pressure layer that never fails the player.
What hurts:
- The win shot leaves Pip out.
- Grading is trivially A for every route, wrecking included, so the clean and chaos routes have no scoring identity.
- Letting go (Q) has no target or payoff in this room, and no bonus rewards chaos.
- The strip-first order creates lots of back-and-forth walking before the fun starts.
- Coworkers have no colliders, so the most obvious slapstick (bumping blobs, bonking them with thrown mugs) can't happen.
DR-03: on the tidy path, nothing funny happens in the first 30 s unless the player throws things. Throwing a bin at a pod did alarm 5 coworkers (via the cabinet impact), but throwing the light strip produced no reaction.
notes.clarity:
The objective card plus one-line prompt stays within the ~25-word budget (the start shot has about 20 words). The progress dots and stars read well at 1440×900 and on the phone (shot 46). Strain colours read without text, and the HUD length bar is clear. Clarity problems:
- The card and prompt disagree at the start ('Pick up the plug' vs 'Fetch the power strip'), after placement ('Grab the power strip'), and at the heater ('Unplug the kettle').
- 'Grab the thing' appears for the vending machine and the glass.
- The marker has no outline and no off-screen indicator, and sits on Pip's helmet when the target is at Pip's feet (shot 04).
- The idle hint dots point at the door during the strip step.
- The sprint trick is unhinted, and the stall prompt pushes the player to let go instead.
- Three identical yellow reels (anchor, mail cart, coffee) follow three different rules.
- The lounge beanbag uses job yellow.
- The result card's bonus lines are small (about 12 px), and the card doesn't say which axis earned the A.
notes.models:
Secondary for this pass:
- The kettle on its side table, the fan heater and the coiled cords are readable and charming at zoom 9 (shot 77). The heater is a fairly plain box with a grille, about 3 cues.
- The strip prefab is good (four sockets plus a red reset) but is hidden under the leftover socket box once placed.
- The load gauge has no housing or mount and floats.
- The coupler is a plain teal block.
- Coworker blobs, desks, pillars and cabinets hold up well at zoom 9 and in orbit.
- Coffee steam is soft now but still reads as a large pale balloon at zoom 9 (shot 85).
- The plug rises into Pip's raised left mitt beside the helmet at high strain (shot 16), close to DR-65.
- The dropped second reel sinks into the anchor reel, which has no collider (shot 32).
